name: Bouncing Balls on Parabolic Curve - Divergence Study
description: Two balls falling under gravity and bouncing elastically off a parabolic boundary y = x². Starting from nearly identical initial conditions, we study when and how their trajectories diverge due to the nonlinear bouncing dynamics.
governing_laws: Free fall under gravity between bounces
Momentum and energy conservation at collisions

system_description.motion_type: Free ballistic motion with elastic bounces
system_description.collision_type: Specular reflection (angle in = angle out, relative to normal)

equations.energy_conservation: E = (1/2)m(vₓ² + vᵧ²) + mgy = constant between bounces

divergence_definition.criterion: Balls have diverged when d(t) > threshold_factor × d(0)
divergence_definition.physical_meaning: When spatial separation exceeds 100× initial separation, trajectories are considered divergent
divergence_definition.alternative_criterion: Different bounce count (balls hit different parts of parabola)

elastic_reflection_physics.description: When ball hits curve at point (x_c, x_c²)

study_objectives: Implement accurate collision detection with parabolic boundary
Track two balls with nearly identical initial conditions
Measure divergence time for various initial separations
expected_behavior: Both balls fall and bounce repeatedly
Small differences amplified by nonlinear bounce dynamics
After several bounces, trajectories become uncorrelated
Divergence time increases as initial separation decreases
System exhibits sensitive dependence on initial conditions
visualization_requirements: Animate both balls bouncing on the parabola
Plot divergence time vs initial separation

numerical_considerations.integration_method: RK45 or DOP853 with event detection
